title: Hybrid sales rise while battery electric sales remain lower after tax credit expiration
summary: In the third quarter of 2026 (3Q26), 23% of new light-duty vehicles sold in the United States were hybrid electric, battery electric, or plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, down slightly from 24% in 3Q25. Between 3Q25 and 3Q26, hybrid electric vehicles continued to gain market share, reaching 16% of light-duty vehicle sales. Growth of hybrid electric vehicle sales has slowed this quarter as the average transaction price for a new vehicle passed $50,000-the first time this price has been reached so far this year, according to Kelley Blue Book.

title: U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

title: Data breaches, identity theft, and revocation: a real-world case study on why W3C is developing Verifiable Credential Barcodes
summary: In September 2026, journalists reported what may be one of the largest breaches of government-issued identity documents in history. Cybercrime enables document fraud at an unprecedented scale, and cryptographic security on physical documents in the form of digital signatures is not enough. Real-time revocation is needed to protect individuals against identity theft. W3C Verifiable Credential Barcodes could be one solution - and the technology is open and free for all to use.

title: Category 2 Hurricane Isaias nears landfall, leading to production shut-ins
summary: As of 4:00 a.m. central time on October 9, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration expects Hurricane Isaias to make landfall on the Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, creating the potential for significant disruptions to energy infrastructure.
